body:
BUG-1303 now reproduces NOWHERE, and I could not find a change that explains it — which makes the disposition a real question rather than a formality

Your Windows result plus the lane's Linux stress runs leave the defect with no reproduction on any platform:

  Windows   run 35499761021 — tick_lock_is_nonblocking_and_reusable PASSES (you read the full log, not an absence)
  Linux     200 stress runs — not reproduced
  macOS     green

Two independent failures on 2026-09-19 — one deterministic on Windows, one a flake on Linux under parallel load — and neither reproduces today.

I WENT LOOKING FOR THE CHANGE THAT FIXED IT AND DID NOT FIND ONE. Since the first Windows failure, exactly one commit touched maintenance_schedule.rs:

  0cf15d6c9e  fix(cli): honor --format json ... (BUG-1289)   2 insertions

I read its diff against that file. It does not touch the lock, the try-lock call, the tick path or the test. And `git log -S try_lock` over aida-cli-lib since then returns nothing. So no change I can find accounts for the Windows reproduction disappearing.

THAT IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART. A deterministic platform failure that stops reproducing with no identifiable cause has two readings, and they want opposite dispositions:

  (a) something incidental changed the timing — a dependency, a runner image, ordering under a different test count —
      and the defect is still there, now intermittent on Windows as well as Linux. Closing it loses a real bug and the
      evidence that found it.
  (b) it was environmental on the runner all along, and both failures were the same infrastructure noise wearing
      two costumes. Keeping it open funds speculative fixes for a defect that does not exist — which is exactly
      what round 1 produced.

I do not think we can distinguish these from what we have, and I would rather say that than pick the comfortable one.

WHAT I WOULD DO, and it is your call. Keep requirement 1 exactly as written — establish the cause — but change what satisfies it. Right now it reads as "determine which hypothesis holds", which assumes a reproduction exists. It cannot be met. Let "we ran X on Y and Z and it does not reproduce, here are the commands and conditions, cause undetermined" satisfy it, and let the spec close on that evidence rather than on a fix.

That is not giving up. A recorded non-reproduction with stated conditions is genuinely useful: when this recurs — and a timing-dependent lock bug usually does — the next person starts from "it went quiet on 2026-09-20 with no code change" instead of rediscovering everything. A speculative EINTR patch would have destroyed that starting point by making the symptom ambiguous.

WHAT I WOULD NOT DO: merge the EINTR handling as-is. Your point stands unchanged — a Windows pass cannot confirm a hypothesis about a Linux race, and now there is no failure anywhere for it to be the fix for.

ONE PROCESS NOTE. The two other Windows failures you saw are both known and neither is BUG-1303's: the pull-rebase test whose fix sits unmerged in #1977, and whatever the second was. That #1977 fix has now been proven on Windows, withdrawn from its original hold reason, and is still not merged — so every cross-platform run keeps carrying a failure we fixed yesterday. It is making these logs harder to read for everyone, including you just now.
